You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: every wrong submission costs 1 and every demo request costs 1. An
instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

### Additional confirmed instance (task-761f6fb6, 13x11)
Background was color 3 and row marks were color 6. Fill only the color-3 cells strictly between consecutive 6s in each row with color 2; preserve the marks and all cells outside each consecutive-mark span. This test had rows with alternating marks/background, including four marks (thus fill three internal gaps), as well as other rows with 2–3 marks, and two rows were unaffected because they had no marks. A 3-mark row separated by regular one-cell gaps became alternating `6,2,6,2,6`; the 4-mark row became `6,2,6,2,6,2,6`. Accepted with zero wrong attempts. Process each row independently; multiple internal gaps are all filled, but never extend past the first or last mark.

### Additional confirmed instance (task-761f6fb6, 27x15)
Background color 9; marks color 8. Each row is handled independently: replace only color-9 cells strictly between consecutive color-8 marks with 2. Preserve all 8 marks and all 9 cells before the first and after the last mark; rows with no marks are unchanged. Confirmed output on a 27x15 grid with varied mark counts (including rows with 2, 3, and 4 marks) was accepted with zero wrong attempts. Useful validation: in the original rows, mark positions can be listed 1-based; fill every gap between adjacent positions only, regardless of gap length.
